problem:
By integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}z{e}^{x}+2y\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,-1\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1}.$

examples.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R z-xy  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

over the rectangular box $R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \:0 \leq x \leq 2, \: -1 \leq y \leq 1, \: 1 \leq z \leq 3 \right\}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} z-xy \: \textrm{d}V
= 
\int_{-1}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} \int_{1}^{3} z-xy \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}y
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ we write $\textrm d V = \textrm d z\:\textrm d x\:\textrm d y.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}z-xy\,dz\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{3}z-xy\,dz]dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}-xyz]}_{z=1}^{z=3}\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(9-1)-xy(3-1)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}4-2xy\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}4-2xy\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}4-2yx\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[4x-y{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}4(2-0)-y({2}^{2}-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}8-4y\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}8-4y\,dy & =[8y-2{y}^{2}]_{y=-1}^{y=1} \\  & =8(1-(-1))-2({1}^{2}-(-1)^{2}) \\  & =8\cdot 2-2(1-1) \\  & =16-0 \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,-1\le y\le 1,\,1\le z\le e}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,\operatorname{ln}⁡3]\times [-1,1]\times [1,e]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{e}^{x}}{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{z}\,\text{d}z & =[{e}^{x}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot [y]_{-1}^{1}\cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡z]_{1}^{e} \\  & =(3-1)\cdot (1-(-1))\cdot (1-0) \\  & =2\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
